title: Fair Value Measurements
description: Analyze fair value measurement concepts, valuation inputs, and the fair value hierarchy.
html:
Fair Value Measurements

Fair value measurement focuses on the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants.

Core Idea:

Fair value is a market-based measurement, not an entity-specific measurement.

1. Exit Price

Fair value is generally based on an exit price.

For an asset, think about the price the company would receive to sell the asset.

For a liability, think about the price the company would pay to transfer the liability.

Asset Price Received to Sell
Liability Price Paid to Transfer

2. Principal Market

Fair value is generally measured using the principal market for the asset or liability.

The principal market is the market with the greatest volume and level of activity for the asset or liability.

3. Most Advantageous Market

If there is no principal market, the entity generally considers the most advantageous market to which it has access.

This is the market that maximizes the amount received to sell an asset or minimizes the amount paid to transfer a liability, after considering transaction costs.

4. Transaction Costs

Transaction costs are generally not included as an adjustment to the fair value measurement itself because they are not an attribute of the asset or liability.

Transportation costs are different when location is an attribute of the asset.

CPA Distinction:

Transaction costs generally do not reduce fair value, but necessary transportation costs may affect the measurement when location is an asset characteristic.

5. Fair Value Hierarchy

Valuation inputs are classified into three levels.

Level 1 Quoted Prices in Active Markets
Level 2 Other Observable Inputs
Level 3 Unobservable Inputs

Level 1 Inputs

Level 1 inputs are quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the reporting entity can access at the measurement date.

Example

A company owns publicly traded shares. The identical shares have an observable quoted market price on an active exchange.

That quoted price is generally a Level 1 input.

Level 2 Inputs

Level 2 includes observable inputs other than quoted Level 1 prices.

Examples may include:

  • Quoted prices for similar assets
  • Observable interest rates
  • Yield curves
  • Other market-corroborated inputs

Level 3 Inputs

Level 3 inputs are unobservable inputs used when relevant observable market information is not available.

These measurements may rely more heavily on valuation models and assumptions that market participants would use.

Example

A highly specialized asset has no active market and little observable market data. Management uses a valuation model containing significant unobservable assumptions.

Those significant assumptions are generally Level 3 inputs.

6. Valuation Techniques

Common approaches used to measure fair value include:

Market Approach Market Transaction Information
Income Approach Present Value / Future Amounts
Cost Approach Current Replacement Capacity

CPA Exam Memory Rule

Level 1 → Identical + Active Market Level 2 → Observable Level 3 → Unobservable

Key Takeaways

  • Fair value is generally an exit-price measurement.
  • Fair value reflects assumptions of market participants.
  • The principal market is generally used when one exists.
  • Level 1 provides quoted prices for identical items in active markets.
  • Level 2 consists primarily of other observable inputs.
  • Level 3 consists of unobservable inputs.
  • The hierarchy prioritizes observable market information over unobservable assumptions.

quiz.prompt: A company owns shares of publicly traded common stock. An unadjusted quoted price for identical shares is available in an active market that the company can access on the measurement date. What level of the fair value hierarchy does this input represent?

choices.text: The input is outside the fair value hierarchy

quiz.explanation: An unadjusted quoted price in an active market for an identical asset that the entity can access is a Level 1 input.
